column2: Germany shares the Eurozone's single currency and interest rate with France and Italy. Each member's own Taylor Rule reading pulls the shared rate toward its own inflation and labour-market situation (its unemployment against its structural rate), weighted by its share of the three countries' household spending at current prices - the basis Eurostat weights the euro area's inflation index on. As Germany's governor you get a modest, bounded push on top of that blend - real influence, not unilateral control, the same way no single member state sets the ECB's rate alone.
